summary.intent: Run Session 2 of the v1-alpha launch plan: ship WP D (init branch/workflow boundary), then J (twine OIDC env) and L (publish isolation across generated release workflows), following lead decisions and review findings.
summary.outcome: WP D shipped as merged PR #565 with both findings resolved; J's first piece is up as PR #569. L is fully implemented and gate-green in its worktree (55 files) and staged with a commit message written, but not yet committed, mutated, reviewed-after-fixes, pushed or linked to trail #459; J's docs and changeset are also pending.

repo: Placeholders in the workflow templates (__BRANCH__, __COMMIT__, __VERSION__) must be substituted in a single pass that never rescans inserted values, or a branch named __BRANCH__ re-expands; generated branch names are always JSON-double-quoted and +/! are escaped in trigger filters via WorkflowScalar.

BranchName in callisto-model identity.rs is re-exported via glob, and git ref parsing must strip the full refs/heads/ or refs/remotes/origin/ prefix rather than take the last '/' segment, so release/next survives.
callisto-model has its own Version type, so callisto-cli does not need a semver dependency.
Gate recipes are just pre-push, lint, doc-check, test and ci, which must be judged by exit code; builds run with CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 and one at a time per worktree.

cargo mutants is used as `--in-place --in-diff <diff> --test-tool nextest`; it uses the worktree, so no edits can happen while it runs, and mutants.out* dirs must be gitignored (changed to mutants.out*/).
Insta snapshot tests pin rendered workflow bytes in callisto-graph init snapshots; they must be reviewed when templates change.
Existing error codes are reused rather than adding new ones (E304 for unsupported artifact owner, E306/E308/E309 generalized); new JSON keys or codes need lead approval.
`cargo package -p a` fails when crate a depends on an unpublished sibling of the same release; verification needs all crates at once (`cargo package -p a -p b --locked`).
Architecture tests (callisto-graph --test architecture) forbid apply permits from literals; the cli init.rs needed a fix for that.

Branch/PR protocol: signed commits, explicit-refspec pushes verified with git ls-remote, `entire trail link <n> --base main`, `entire trail ci-pr`, and `entire trail finding add/resolve`; no stacked PRs, so dependent work waits for merge.

code.finding: NpmRegistry::publish ignored its artifact-manifest argument and published from the checkout; L changes it to publish only the sealed tarball after re-hashing, with E306 when unsealed.
render_init prints '[DRY-RUN] Would write' whenever initialized is false, so the workflow-only path had to report initialized: true on real writes.
Matrix generation drops artifacts with non-Cargo owners, which makes the release fail with 'callisto matrix has no entry for artifact slot', so retry-path init must reject them.
detect_facts re-synthesizes config rather than reading the user's callisto.toml, causing false E193/E194 on workflow-only retry; fixed by detecting from the existing config.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user authority, and claims must be checked against source (e.g. the design's per-crate cargo package assumption was false).
Delegating implementation to a subagent while keeping gating, review and shipping in the main session works when context is heavily used, but the main session must re-run the gate itself.
BSD sed on macOS mishandles some escaped replacements; the Edit tool or python -I scripts are safer for multi-line or quoted edits.
EnterWorktree should be called with name= rather than path= to avoid the relocation prompt.
Mutation testing on the diff caught real test gaps (e.g. `||`→`&&` mutants), and timeouts from non-terminating loops count as kills.
A run of cargo fmt after the last gate invalidates earlier doc-check/test results, so gates must be re-run on the formatted commit.

friction: Worktree-entry prompts stopped the session and caused a resume in the wrong worktree, producing a mistaken J worktree nested inside D's that had to be removed and recreated as the `worktree-wp-j-twine-env2` branch.
Rules forbidding stacked PRs blocked L until #565 merged, leaving the session idle.
The auto-mode classifier denied npx fetches of yarn and bun, leaving their pack flags unverified; corepack and Verdaccio are not installed.
Repeated identical commands (git fetch, status) and a git add -A mistake from the wrong directory needed retries; cargo fmt after the gate forced re-running checks.
The research JSONs were untracked in the main checkout, so F09 context had to be read from there and /tmp.
The implementer subagent reported interim and then final results in two hand-backs, and its first report contained a deferral (D2) later reversed by lead decision.
open_items: L is staged but uncommitted: still needs the signed commit, cargo mutants --in-diff, a fresh Opus review of the final diff, explicit-refspec push, trail #459 link and entire trail ci-pr.

J (#569) still needs the trusted-publishing recipe with Node 22.14+/npm 11.5.1+ setup step, docs/publishing.md updates, and a changeset; the rest of J (PYPI_TOKEN optional, crates.io auth step) follows.
WP D's PR body lacks the sibling-sweep notes, and just ci was never run for D.
Matrix execute never maps NPM_TOKEN/PYPI_TOKEN into .npmrc or TWINE_*; filed as a finding on trail #459 for its own PR after J.
Out-of-scope findings filed on #459: publint/packed-content validation, and npm staged publishing.

Unverified: yarn pack --out and bun pm pack flags, npm publish <tgz> --provenance, attest-build-provenance glob subject-path, gh attestation verify, the Linux-only Verdaccio e2e (does not compile here), and no generated workflow run on real GitHub Actions.
cargo package -p from workspace root does not cover crates in nested cargo workspaces.
credentials_needed_by in runner.rs is unchanged, so pnpm/yarn/bun lockfile refresh and install in `callisto version` may still need NPM_TOKEN for private registries.
Yarn/bun registry config via .yarnrc.yml or bun config is no longer read because npm publishes; documented as a limit only.
Tarball name/version check uses reading package/package.json with system tar; a prepack rewriting after pack is caught only at confirmation.
#569 merge is ordered after L per the lead; owner-policy items (ruleset bypass, immutable releases) stay with the lead.
